Thanks for the demo this morning — it was helpful to see latency/cost controls in action. A few follow-ups from our privacy/security team so we can qualify Redwood for our POC:

- Can you confirm whether observability/telemetry events sent to third-party vendors contain any PII or user-identifying keys? We need an explicit statement.
- What is your default logging retention for request traces and error payloads? Can that be reduced for sensitive tenants?
- We run parts of our stack in a marketplace flow (3rd-party marketplace connector). How do you classify subprocessors in that path (Redwood + marketplace partner + downstream analytics vendor)?

Hi Alice — great to meet you and thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; I'll follow with a short dataflow sketch and a more formal subprocessors appendix for your risk team.

1) PII in telemetry: Our observability pipelines are designed to avoid PII by default. Application-level logs sent to our hosted telemetry plugin are treated as unstructured logs; we recommend that customers redact user identifiers client-side. For any optional structured telemetry (e.g., event attributes), Redwood will not surface raw user_id or email fields to downstream analytics vendors unless explicitly enabled by the customer. We can provide a signed statement for procurement.

2) Retention: Default trace/error retention is 30 days for hosted observability data; aggregated metrics are stored 90 days. We support tenant-level retention overrides (down to 7 days) on Dedicated and Private deployments.

3) Marketplace/subprocessor classification: In a marketplace flow, parties typically look like: Customer (you) -> Marketplace connector (Marketplace Partner) -> Redwood inference + observability -> downstream analytics vendor (if enabled). For clarity, Redwood lists both the marketplace connector and any third-party analytics as subprocessors when telemetry forwarding is configured. We'll deliver a delta appendix showing which subprocessors receive exported telemetry.

I'll attach a simple dataflow sketch and our current subprocessors appendix (redacted to public-facing names) so your security team can thumb through. Next steps I propose: (a) we send a short proc/security pack to your SecOps; (b) Marissa will scope an on-prem/KMS option if you need tenant-specific keys; (c) can we schedule a quick 30-min call with your security lead tomorrow?

Best,
Priyom Das
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Hi — answers and next steps inline below. I've also uploaded the signed statement and a scrubbed subprocessor mapping to the Drive link.

- Config flag: We expose a telemetry_forwarding.enabled boolean at the tenant config level (Hosted API defaults to false). When set to false, no observability payloads are forwarded to downstream analytics vendors. We'll include this flag and its API path in contract language.

- Header stripping: Redwood's telemetry agent strips Authorization, Cookie, and Set-Cookie headers by default before any forwarding. Customers can opt in to include specified headers but it must be explicit and documented.

- Retention + backups: Retention policy applies to primary observability stores. Backups are retained according to region policy; however, on Dedicated/Private we support alignment to your retention SLA (we can commit to 7 days for the POC environment and provide evidence exports).

Attachments uploaded: redwood-subprocessors-appendix.pdf (public redacted), redwood-dataflow-sketch.png (visual).
